source.title: Extra extension properties of equidimensional holomorphic mappings: results and open questions

accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact Kähler surface, let B* = B \ {0} be the punctured ball, and let f: B* → X be a locally biholomorphic mapping. Suppose f extends meromorphically to the whole ball B, and let E := f̂[0] be the full image of the origin under this meromorphic extension. Prove that E is an exceptional curve in X.
accepted.context_brief: Extension of punctured-ball maps to compact Kähler surfaces

evidence.quote: Let X be a compact K¨ahler surface and let f : B∗ → X be a locally biholomorphic mapping of the punctured ball B∗ = B \ {0} into X. Then f extends meromorphically onto the whole ball B. The full image by the extension f̂ of the origin denote by E := f̂[0]. Question 2.1 Prove that E is an exceptional curve in X.

accepted.question_text: In the setting of Theorem 2.4, let X be a compact infinitesimally homogeneous Kähler manifold, let D be a domain over a Stein manifold, let f: D → X be locally biholomorphic, let f̂: D̂ → X be its meromorphic extension to the envelope of holomorphy D̂, and let I be the indeterminacy set of f̂. Determine what can be said about the image f̂[I].
accepted.context_brief: Indeterminacy image for meromorphic extension in Theorem 2.4

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.4 Let X be a compact infinitesimally homogeneous K¨ahler manifold. Then every locally biholomorphic mapping f : D → X from a domain D over a Stein manifold into X extends to a locally biholomorphic mapping f̂ : D̂ → X of the envelope of holomorphy D̂ of D into X.
Question 2.2 What can be said about f̂[I] in the conditions of Theorem 2.4?

accepted.question_text: Prove the all-dimensional analogue of the extension results discussed in Section 3: meromorphic mappings from the Hartogs figure H_n^k(r) = Δ^n(1 − r) × Δ^k ∪ Δ^n × A^k(r, 1) into compact manifolds or spaces in the classes P_k^- and G_k should extend to Δ^{n+k} \ A, where A has Hausdorff (2n − 1)-dimensional measure zero. In particular, prove that the analogue of Theorem 3.2 should hold for meromorphic mappings between equidimensional manifolds in all dimensions.

evidence.quote: General Conjecture. Meromorphic mappings from Hkn(r) to compact (disk-convex) manifolds of class P−k should extend onto Δn+k \ A where A is of Haussdorf (2n − 1)-dimensional measure zero. If the image manifold is from class Gk then A ≠ ∅ should imply very restrictive conditions on the topology and complex structure of X (see results below).

Question 3.1 We conjecture that the analogous result should hold for meromorphic mappings in all dimensions. I.e. from Hkn(r) to compact manifolds (and spaces) in the classes P−k and Gk. In particular, Theorem 3.2 should be true for meromorphic mappings between equidimensional manifolds in all dimensions.

accepted.question_text: As a first step toward the general conjecture of Question 3.1, prove extension for meromorphic mappings from H_2^2(r) to a manifold of class G_2.
accepted.context_brief: First test case for the general extension conjecture

evidence.quote: Question 3.2 One can start proving the general conjecture (as in Question 3.1) by considering extension from H22(r) to a manifold of class G2.

accepted.question_text: Prove an all-dimensional analogue of Corollary 3.2. In dimension 3, Corollary 3.2 says that if V is a compact affine 3-fold and its universal covering, viewed as a domain over C^3 with locally biholomorphic projection, is pseudoconcave at some boundary point, then V contains a spherical shell of dimension 3. The question asks for the corresponding statement in all dimensions.
accepted.context_brief: All-dimensional analogue of the affine-covering corollary

evidence.quote: Corollary 3.2 Let V be a compact affine 3-fold and let (Ṽ , π) be its universal covering considered as a domain over C3 with locally biholomorphic projection π. Then if (Ṽ , π) is pseudoconcave at some boundary point then V contains a spherical shell (of dimension 3).
Question 3.3 An analog of Corollary 3.2. in all dimensions seems to be an easier problem then the Question 3.1 in its whole generality.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact complex manifold carrying a plurinegative metric form, and let f: Δ^3 \ S → X be a meromorphic mapping. Suppose A is a minimal closed subset of Δ^3 such that f extends to Δ^3 \ A. Prove that each connected component of A is a complex curve.
accepted.context_brief: Structure of the singularity set for plurinegative targets

evidence.quote: Question 3.4 Let X is a compact complex manifold carrying a plurinegative metric form, and let f : Δ3 \ S → X is a meromorphic mapping. Suppose that A is a minimal closed subset of Δ3 such that f extends onto Δ3 \ A. Prove that each connected component of A is a complex curve.

accepted.question_text: Let {X_t} be a complex deformation of compact complex manifolds. Assume that every fiber X_t with t ≠ 0 has the meromorphic extension property, meaning that every meromorphic map from a domain in a Stein manifold extends meromorphically to the envelope of holomorphy of the domain. Does the central fiber X_0 also have the meromorphic extension property?
accepted.context_brief: Persistence of the meromorphic extension property in the limit fiber

evidence.quote: Let’s give the formal statement. We say that a complex manifold X possesses a meromorphic extension property if for every domain D in Stein manifold every meromorphic mapping f : D → X meromorphically extends onto the envelope of holomorphy of D.
Question 4.1 Suppose all Xt for t ≠ 0 possed meromorphic extension property (as, for example, K¨ahler manifolds). Does X0 possesses it as well?

accepted.question_text: Let {X_t} be a complex deformation of compact complex manifolds. If the central fiber X_0 has the meromorphic extension property, does every nearby fiber X_t also have the meromorphic extension property?
accepted.context_brief: Openness of the meromorphic extension property under deformation

evidence.quote: We say that a complex manifold X possesses a meromorphic extension property if for every domain D in Stein manifold every meromorphic mapping f : D → X meromorphically extends onto the envelope of holomorphy of D.
Question 4.2 If X0 possesses a mer. ext. prop. does Xt possesses it for t close to zero?

accepted.question_text: Let D ⊂ CP^3 cover a compact complex threefold X, and let Λ := CP^3 \ D. Proposition 5.1, Case 1 says that if Λ is locally a finite union of two-dimensional submanifolds, then Λ is a union of finitely many lines. Prove an analogue of that conclusion assuming only that the 2-dimensional Hausdorff measure h_2(Λ) is finite; in that case the components of Λ may be lines and points.
accepted.context_brief: Large domains in CP^3 with finite h_2 boundary

evidence.quote: Proposition 5.1 Suppose a domain D ⊂ CP3 covers a compact complex threefold X. Case 1. If the complement Λ = CP3 \ D is locally a finite union of two-dimensional submanifolds, then Λ is a union of finitely many lines.
Question 5.1 Prove an analog of the Case 1 of Theorem 5.1 assuming only that h2(Λ) is finite. In that case the components of Λ could be lines and points.

accepted.question_text: Let D ⊂ CP^3 cover a compact complex threefold, and let Λ := CP^3 \ D be locally a union of four-dimensional submanifolds. Must every component of Λ be either a complex hypersurface or a CR-submanifold of CR-dimension one? Can components occur that are not CR-submanifolds? If CR-submanifold components do occur, are they Levi-flat?
accepted.context_brief: Geometry of four-dimensional boundary components in CP^3

evidence.quote: Question 5.2 Suppose that the complement Λ = CP3 \ D is locally a union of four-dimensional submanifolds. Are all components of Λ necessariry either complex hypersurfaces or CR-manifolds of CR-dimension one? Or, one can have components which are not CR-submanifolds? Are those CR-submanifolds Levi-flat?

accepted.question_text: Can every complex surface be embedded as a subdomain of a disk-convex complex surface?
accepted.context_brief: Embedding complex surfaces into disk-convex surfaces

evidence.quote: Question 6.1 Can every complex surface be imbedded as a subdomain into a disk-convex complex surface?

accepted.question_text: Compare the notion of disk-convexity in Definition 6.1 with the alternative notions listed in Section 6.4: (i) for every compact K ⊂ X there is a compact K̂ such that every holomorphic map from a bordered Riemann surface (R, ∂R) into X with boundary in K has image in K̂; (ii) every sequence of analytic disks that converges on ∂Δ also converges on the closed disk Δ̄; and (iii) the analogous convergence statement for sequences of Riemann surfaces instead of disks. What are the logical relations among these notions, and are they equivalent to Definition 6.1?

evidence.quote: Definition 6.1 (a) Complex space X is called disk-convex if for every compact K ⊂ X there is another compact K̂ such that if for any holomorphic map h : Δ̄ → X with h(∂Δ) ⊂ K one has h(Δ) ⊂ K̂. (b) X is called disk-convex in dimension k if for every compact K ⊂ X there is another compact K̂ such that if for any meromorphic map h : Δ̄k → X with h(∂Δk) ⊂ K one has h(Δk) ⊂ K̂.

i) A complex manifold X is said to be disk-convex if for any compact K ⊂ X there exists a compact K̂ ⊂ X such that for every Riemann surface with boundary (R, ∂R) and every holomorphic mapping φ : R → X continuous up to the boundary the condition φ(∂R) ⊂ K imply φ(R) ⊂ K̂. ii) X is called disk-convex if for any convergent on ∂Δ sequence {φn : Δ̄ → X} of analytic disks this sequence converge also on Δ̄. iii) The same definition can be given with sequences of Riemann surfaces instead of the disk. Question 6.2 What is the relation between all these notions and that defined in Definition 6.1? Are they equivalent?

accepted.question_text: Let D be the two-sheeted cover of Δ^2 \ R^2, so D is a nonschlicht domain over C^2. Does there exist a compact complex manifold X and a holomorphic or meromorphic mapping f: D → X that separates points? The paper further notes that any such X cannot carry a plurinegative metric form, so examples, if they exist, would have to begin in complex dimension greater than 3.
accepted.context_brief: Separating-point maps from a nonschlicht domain over C^2

evidence.quote: Question 7.1 Let the complex manifold D is defined as two-sheeted cover of Δ2 \ R2, i.e. D is a "nonschlicht" domain over C2. Does there exist a compact complex manifold X and a holomorphic (meromorphic) mapping f : D → X which separates points? Note that the results of this paper imply that such X if exists cannot possed a plurinegative metric form. Thus examples could occur starting from dim X > 3.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact complex space equipped with a Hermitian metric form ω, and consider the class J_R of meromorphic mappings f: Δ^k → X such that the norm of the differential satisfies ||Df|| > R > 0 and the image volume satisfies Vol(f(Δ^k)) ≤ C_1 for all f in J_R. Prove that there exists a constant C_2 = C_2(X, R, C_1) such that the graph volume Vol(Γ_f) is at most C_2 for every f in J_R.
accepted.context_brief: Uniform graph-volume bounds from differential and image-volume bounds

evidence.quote: Question 7.2 Consider a class JR of meromorphic mappings f : Δk → X, X being compact, such that (a) ||Df|| > R > 0. Here ||Df|| denotes the norm of the differential of f; (b) Vol(f(Δk)) ≤ C1 for all f ∈ JR. Prove that there is a constant C2 = C2(X, R, C1) such that Vol(Γf) ≤ C2 for all f ∈ JR.

accepted.question_text: Let f: Δ_*^k → X be a meromorphic mapping from a punctured polydisk into a compact complex space X. Assume the image volume is finite: Vol(f(Δ_*^k)) < ∞. Prove that f extends meromorphically across the puncture at 0.

evidence.quote: Question 7.3 Let f : Δ∗k → X be a meromorphic mapping from a punctured polydisk into a compact complex space X. Suppose that Volf(Δ∗k) < ∞. Prove that f meromorphically extends to zero.

accepted.question_text: Fix 0 < r < 1, a constant R, and a compact complex space X. Let F_R be the class of meromorphic maps f: Δ^n → X such that (1) the 2n-dimensional volume of the part of the graph Γ_f lying over the annulus A^n(r, 1) is at most R, and (2) for every k-disk Δ_z^k = {z} × Δ^k with z ∈ Δ^{n-k}, the 2k-dimensional volume of the part of the restricted graph Γ_{f_z} lying over the annulus A_z^k(r, 1) is at most R. Prove both directions: first, for every constant l there is a constant A such that if f ∈ F_R and Vol_{2k}(Γ_{f_z}) ≤ l for all restrictions to k-disks, then Vol_{2n}(Γ_f) ≤ A; second, for every constant a there is a constant L such that if f ∈ F_R and Vol_{2n}(Γ_f) ≤ a, then Vol_{2k}(Γ_{f_z}) ≤ L for all k-disks Δ_z^k.
accepted.context_brief: Relating global and slice graph-volume bounds under annular control

evidence.quote: Question 7.5 Fix some 0 < r < 1 and some constant R. Fix also a compact complex space X. Consider the following class FR of meromorphic mappings from f : Δn → X: (1) Vol2n(Γf ∩ (An(r, 1) × X)) ≤ R; (2) for every k-disk Δzk = {z} × Δk ( where z ∈ Δn−k) Vol2k(Γfz ∩ Akz(r, 1) × X) ≤ R. Prove that for any constant l there is a constant A such that for any f ∈ FR satisfying Vol2k(Γfz) ≤ l for all restrictions fz onto the k-disks Δzk one has Vol2n(Γf) ≤ A. (b) Vice versa: for any constant a there is a constant L such that for any f ∈ FR such that Vol2n(Γf) ≤ a one has Vol2k(Γfs) ≤ L for all Δzk.

accepted.question_text: Let F be a family of holomorphic or meromorphic mappings from the unit polydisk Δ^{n+1} to a compact Kähler manifold X, or more generally to a compact complex target X in the class G_1. Suppose F is equicontinuous on the Hartogs figure H_n^1(r) = Δ^n(1 − r) × Δ ∪ Δ^n × A^1(r, 1). Must F then be equicontinuous on the whole polydisk Δ^{n+1}?
accepted.context_brief: Equicontinuity propagation from a Hartogs figure

evidence.quote: Consider the Hartogs figure Hkn(r) := Δn(1 − r) × Δk ∪ Δn × Ak(r, 1) ⊂ Cn+k.

Question 7.7 Let F be some family of holomorphic (meromorphic) mappings from the unit polydisk Δn+1 to a compact K¨ahler manifold X (or X ∈ G1 more generally). Suppose that F is equicontinuous on the Hartogs figure H1n(r). Will F be equicontinuous on Δn+1?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Question 7.4 Let f : Δ∗k+1 → X ∈ Gk be a meromorphic map from punctured (k + 1)-disk into a compact complex space from class Gk. Prove that Vol(f(Ak(r, 1)) = O(logkk−1(1/r)) provided k > 2. In particular for equidimensional maps f : Δ∗n → Xn one always should have Vol(f(An(r, 1)) = O(lognn−1(1/r)).

evidence.quote: Question 7.4 Let f : Δk+1∗ → X ∈ Gk be a meromorphic map from punctured (k + 1)-disk into a compact complex space from class Gk. Prove that Vol(f(Ak(r, 1)) = O(logkk−1 (1/r)) provided k > 2. In particular for equidimensional maps f : Δn∗ → Xn one always should have Vol(f(An(r, 1)) = O(lognn−1 (1/r)).

needs_review.question_text_raw: Question 7.6 Let X = {Xt} be a deformation of compact complex surfaces. Suppose that Xt for t ≠ 0 contain a global spherical shell. Does X0 contain a GSS?

evidence.quote: Question 7.6 Let X = {Xt} be a deformation of compact complex surfaces. Suppose that Xt for t ≠ 0 contain a global spherical shell. Does X0 contain a GSS?
